A.title: Ring-fenced landlord claim fee, plus early settlement before court
A.answer: Keep the county courts and the Section 21 ban. Claims rose 21% to 28,249 and accelerated claims 68% to 12,156 (s1), while the Law Society says courts are under-resourced (s2). The Ministry of Justice would raise the landlord claim fee and ring-fence the money for judges and court staff, so tenants and rent-payers carry no extra cost. Landlords would have to offer a settlement step, such as mediation or a payment plan, before issuing, with the fee refunded if the case settles. Tenants keep full hearings. Check each quarter in the Ministry statistics: median claim-to-possession time (25.9 weeks, s2) should fall while completed repossessions (6,886, s1) do not collapse, and settled cases should rise.

B.title: Move eviction claims to a dedicated housing tribunal
B.answer: Possession claims rose 21% to 28,249 in a quarter, with accelerated claims up 68% to a record 12,156 (s1, s3). Today they compete with every other county court case. The Ministry of Justice should move landlord possession claims out of the general courts into a dedicated housing tribunal with its own judges, staff and budget, so other cases stop queuing behind them. It would also run free early mediation for both sides before a hearing. The Law Society says the courts are not resourced for the increase (s2). We would know it worked if completed repossessions, down 10% to 6,886 (s1), recover, waits stay near 25.9 weeks or fall (s2), and the tribunal reports on both.
